cases.comment: POSITIVE, and the case that caught the author out: 'azaltabileceğini düşündürmektedir' carries TWO hedges and still lands above an associative card, because the demotion is one rung and 4 - 1 = 3 > 1. Cases 035-037 pin the boundary so the rule cannot drift into flagging properly qualified prose.

mutations.breaks: Hedged prose stops being recognised as hedged, so a properly qualified sentence is scored at its bare verb's rung and reported as an overclaim.
A sentence reporting the study's own work stops being exempt from the citation requirement, so every Results sentence becomes an uncited assertion.
'as Table 2 shows' stops counting as in-manuscript evidence, so pointing at the author's own figure is flagged as needing an external citation.
A percentage, p-value or CI stops registering as an empirical signal, so the strongest uncited-assertion shape goes unreported.
English nominalized claims stop carrying a rung, so 'the effect of X on Y' / 'the driver of Y' written over an associative card is no longer an overclaim.
The nominal patterns stop requiring 'of'/'on' after the noun, so meta-analysis vocabulary ('effect size', 'random-effects model') is swept up as a relational claim.
The Turkish nominal 'etkisi' stops carrying rung 4, restoring the asymmetry where an English nominal was scored and its Turkish twin was not.
'etkisiz' (the privative: no effect) starts matching the rung-4 nominal, so a sentence denying an effect is reported as an overclaim.
Turkish nominal causation ('nedeni', 'sebebiyle', 'kaynaklanmaktadır') stops carrying rung 5, leaving the verb phrase 'neden ol-' as the only recognised spelling of a causal claim.
The bare noun 'katkısı' stops carrying rung 3, so a contribution claim counts only when written with one of the light verbs.

A Roman-numeral section cross-reference stops counting as an own-work pointer, so a manuscript numbered I./II./III./IV. has every self-referring Results sentence in its Discussion reported as an uncited empirical assertion.
